test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: An article is sold for x. If it is sold at 40% of this price, there is a loss of 50%. What is the percentage profit when it is sold for ₹x?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **selling price** x = 100.

New Selling Price = 40% of 100 = 40.

Loss is 50%, so **Cost Price** (CP) = 40 ÷ (1 − 0.50) = 80.

Profit at price x = 100 − 80 = 20.

Profit % = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: SP₁ = x | SP₂ = 0.40x | Loss% = 50%
Formulas: CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%) | Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c5735d8cfd50e3573d8c6cc601a8129721eb03b6bffe3c8e7b2634778b25939.png] 
⇒ When sold at 0.40x, Loss = 50%, so CP = 0.40x ÷ 0.50 = 0.80x.
⇒ To find profit when sold at x: Profit = x − 0.80x = 0.20x.
⇒ Profit % = (0.20x ÷ 0.80x) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price and Cost Price Relationship

If an object is sold at a **loss**, the CP is always greater than the SP. Formula: CP = SP + Loss.

Profit Percentage

Profit percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise. Formula: (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.</p
